App.Title: Little Big Mouse
Main.ExitConfirm.Title: Exit LittleBigMouse?
Main.ExitConfirm.Message: LittleBigMouse will stop controlling mouse transitions until it is started again.
Control.Location.OpenVirtual.Tooltip: View a layout exported by another user, without the hardware. Display only: it cannot be loaded as your own layout.
Control.Location.StartTooltipDetail.Virt: Send this layout to the daemon for validation. The input hook stays off — a foreign layout never drives the local mouse.
Control.Location.StartTooltipDetail.Live: Live update is on: your changes are already being felt, but none of them is saved. This keeps them.
Control.Location.StartTooltipDetail.Manu: Save the layout and hand it to the mouse engine. Use the arrow to have changes sent as you make them instead.
Control.Location.AgentMismatch.Badge: The engine is on another layout
Control.Location.AgentMismatch.Tooltip: The mouse engine is working on a different set of displays. Refreshing makes it read them again.
Dialog.Unsaved.Title: Unsaved layout
Dialog.Unsaved.Heading: Your layout has not been saved
Dialog.Unsaved.Body.Leaving: Your changes to the layout will be lost. The mouse engine keeps the layout you last applied.
Dialog.Unsaved.Body.Closing: Your changes stay in LittleBigMouse and come back with the window, but they are not saved: they are lost if LittleBigMouse exits or the computer restarts. The mouse engine keeps the layout you last applied.
Dialog.Unsaved.SaveNote: Live update is on, so this layout is the one currently driving the mouse — saving it keeps what you have been feeling.
Dialog.MonitorWarning.Detach.Title: Detach monitor
Dialog.MonitorWarning.Detach.Heading: Detach this monitor from the desktop?
Dialog.MonitorWarning.Detach.Body: Windows will stop using this monitor: its screen will go black immediately. This change is kept after a restart, and reattaching it from LittleBigMouse does not always succeed.
Dialog.MonitorWarning.Detach.RecoveryTit: To get the monitor back with Windows:
Dialog.MonitorWarning.Detach.Step1: 1. Right-click the desktop and choose Display settings (or open Settings > System > Display).
Dialog.MonitorWarning.Detach.Step2: 2. Select the detached monitor, then under Multiple displays choose 'Extend desktop to this display'. There you can also fix the resolution and refresh rate.
Dialog.MonitorWarning.Detach.Step3: 3. If it is not listed, click 'Detect other display' there, or press Win+P and choose 'Extend'.
Dialog.MonitorWarning.Attach.Title: Attach monitor
Dialog.MonitorWarning.Attach.Heading: Attach this monitor to the desktop?
Dialog.MonitorWarning.Attach.Body: LittleBigMouse will re-enable this monitor with its last saved position, resolution, orientation and refresh rate. If those no longer match your setup, a monitor may receive an unsupported mode or another screen may change resolution.
Dialog.MonitorWarning.Attach.RecoveryTit: If a screen ends up black or misconfigured:
Dialog.MonitorWarning.Primary.Title: Make primary monitor
Dialog.MonitorWarning.Primary.Heading: Make this monitor the primary display?
Dialog.MonitorWarning.Primary.Body: Windows anchors the desktop on the primary display: every monitor position changes, open windows may move, and the taskbar goes to the new primary. LittleBigMouse will re-anchor its layout accordingly.
Dialog.MonitorWarning.Primary.Step1: Use 'Make primary' on the previous monitor, or in Settings > System > Display select it and check 'Make this my main display'.
Dialog.MonitorWarning.ApplyLayout.Title: Apply layout to system
Dialog.MonitorWarning.ApplyLayout.Headin: Apply this layout to the system configuration?
Dialog.MonitorWarning.ApplyLayout.Body: Monitor positions will be recomputed from the physical layout and applied to the system immediately. The system cannot represent bezels or gaps: adjacent monitors become edge-to-edge, aligned on their physical crossing point.
Dialog.MonitorWarning.ApplyLayout.Step1: 1. Rearrange the monitors in the system display settings, or use 'Place from system config' to re-import the system layout into LittleBigMouse.
Dialog.MonitorWarning.Failure.Title: Display change failed
Dialog.MonitorWarning.Failure.Heading: The system could not {0}.
Dialog.MonitorWarning.Failure.Body: LittleBigMouse stopped the operation and restored the last known desktop configuration. No partial monitor layout was intentionally applied.
Dialog.MonitorWarning.Failure.Step1: Open the system display settings and confirm that every monitor is connected and using a supported mode, then try again.
Dialog.MonitorWarning.NotApplied.Title: Layout not applied
Dialog.MonitorWarning.NotApplied.Heading: The layout could not be saved, so it was not applied.
Dialog.MonitorWarning.NotApplied.Body: Applying it would rearrange the displays and then reload the last saved layout, losing this one. Nothing was changed. ({0})
Dialog.MonitorWarning.NotApplied.Step1: Check that LittleBigMouse is running (its icon in the notification area), then try again.
Dialog.MonitorWarning.AdjustScale: Also adjust display scales to match physical sizes
BootFailure.Title: LittleBigMouse could not start
BootFailure.Body: An error stopped LittleBigMouse while it was starting. It will close when you dismiss this window. Your saved layouts are untouched.
BootFailure.LogText.Stderr: This report was also written to the standard error output.
BootFailure.LogText.File: This report was also written to {0}.
Updater.Title: Update Little Big Mouse
Updater.SupportTooltip: If Little Big Mouse is useful to you, support its development on Ko-fi
DefaultMonitor.Exclude.Tooltip: The monitor stays on the desktop but the cursor can never travel onto it — for displays that are not really monitors (pump LCDs, sensor panels…)
AboutMonitor.Tagline: DPI Aware mouse move across screens for Windows 10 / 11
Options.Title: Settings
Options.Elevated.Tooltip: LittleBigMouse is running with elevated privileges and can work over elevated apps.
Options.Support.Description: Free and open source — if it's useful to you, consider buying me a coffee
Options.AutoUpdate.Description: Look for new versions online in the background
Options.LoadAtStartup.Description: Start LittleBigMouse when you sign in
Options.HideTrayIcon.Description: Reopen the window by launching LittleBigMouse again
Options.BoundToAgent.Header: Stop the mouse engine with LittleBigMouse
Options.BoundToAgent.Description: Off: the engine keeps routing the cursor if LittleBigMouse stops, and picks up again when it comes back
Options.StartElevated.Description: Keeps working over elevated apps (admin accounts only; one UAC prompt on manual launch, none at logon)
Options.Priority.Description: Process priority of the mouse engine
Options.VcpControl.Description: Brightness, contrast, inputs and smart-TV remotes over DDC/CI (adds a panel per monitor)
Options.Experimental.Description: Argyll color calibration and smart-TV remote test tools in the VCP panel
Options.DebugTools.Description: Extra tools for troubleshooting, like viewing exported layouts
Options.Algorithm.Description: How the cursor jumps between screens
Options.Algorithm.Strait.Caption: Strait
Options.Algorithm.Cross.Caption: Corner crossing
Options.Algorithm.Cross.Description: In direction-friendly manner, allows traversal through corners.
Options.PauseInGames.Description: Pause crossing while a game captures the mouse
Options.PauseInGames.Tooltip: While a game captures the mouse (hidden or confined cursor), LBM pauses so the game gets clean relative input. Turn off if LBM wrongly stays paused: some apps hide or confine the cursor without being games.
Options.DetectionInterval.Description: Re-check mouse capture while gaming, in ms
Options.DetectionInterval.Tooltip: Lower values react faster, 0 checks on every mouse event.
Options.AdjustSpeed.Tooltip: Adjust the pointer speed when the system doesn't consider the screens ratio.
Options.AdjustPointer.Tooltip: Adjust the pointer size when the system doesn't consider the screens ratio.
Options.RescueShortcut.Description: Frees the cursor when it gets trapped where you cannot click. Hold it for about a second. One key plus at least one of Ctrl, Alt, Shift or Win.
Options.RescueShortcut.Warning: {0} is already taken by another application — the rescue shortcut is NOT active.
Options.RescueShortcut.Warning.Desktop: Your desktop has not given {0} a key — the rescue shortcut is NOT active. Assign it under "Little Big Mouse" in the desktop's keyboard shortcut settings.
Options.RescueShortcut.Ownership: Your desktop owns global shortcuts: Little Big Mouse asks for this one, and you can change or clear it in the desktop's keyboard shortcut settings.
Options.Touch.Independent.Description: After using the touchscreen, move the mouse to resume from its previous position.
Options.Touch.AllDisplays.Description: Turn off to choose which displays keep the mouse position.
Options.Touch.SelectDisplays: Select displays below. With no selection, the mouse position is not kept on any display.
Options.Touch.Override.Description: Hold this key before tapping to use the touchscreen app normally for that gesture.
Options.AllowOverlaps.Description: Screens may overlap in the layout
Options.MinimalEdgeOverlap.Description: Display surface two touching screens must share, in mm
Options.MinimalEdgeOverlap.Tooltip: When compaction brings two monitors into contact, it guarantees at least this many millimeters of shared display surface along the edge — bezels excluded, the cursor cannot cross them. 0 only asks for contact (a corner counts).
Options.BorderValues.Description: Where each monitor's bezel borders are stored
Options.BorderValues.PerModel.Caption: Per model
Options.BorderValues.PerModel.Descriptio: Borders are shared by all monitors of the same make/model.
Options.BorderValues.PerMonitor.Caption: Per monitor
Options.BorderValues.PerMonitor.Descript: Each physical monitor keeps its own borders.
Options.WarnMonitorActions.Description: Ask for confirmation before attaching, detaching or making a monitor primary
Options.Excluded.Header: LBM pauses when these apps are focused
Options.Excluded.Description: Add a process name or pattern
Options.Excluded.AddDefaultsTooltip: Add the built-in default exclusions (Epic, Steam, Riot, Xbox game folders) that aren't already in the list
Options.SeenProcesses.Description: Click one to use it as pattern
BorderResistance.ShowOnScreensTooltip: Show the sections on the real screens
BorderResistance.MoveTooltip: Resistance in mm opposing a plain cursor move
BorderResistance.DragTooltip: Resistance in mm opposing a move made with a mouse button held
BorderResistance.MirrorTooltip: Copy this section onto the facing edge of the monitor across it
BorderResistance.BlockedNote: This edge is fully blocked in both modes. Ctrl still forces a crossing on Windows and X11, but not on Wayland.
Wallpaper.SpanDescription: One image across all screens, sliced to match the physical layout.
Vcp.LiveRead.Tooltip: Follow changes made on the monitor's own menu: re-read all levels every second, for two minutes.
Vcp.NotAvailable: DDC/CI not available on this monitor.
Vcp.Calibration.Initializing: Initializing instrument — calibration may be requested…
Vcp.Calibration.NotConverged: White point tuning did not converge
Vcp.Remote.PairedConnected: Paired and connected over the local network.
Vcp.Samsung.Subtitle: Samsung Tizen · local network remote
Vcp.Samsung.PictureMacroNote: Picture settings are driven by remote-key macros; Tizen does not expose readable VCP values.
Vcp.Samsung.Status.EnterIp: Enter the monitor IP address or run discovery.
Vcp.Samsung.Status.NoneFound: No Samsung Tizen display found; enter its IP address.
Vcp.Samsung.Status.OneFound: Display found. Select Pair to authorize LittleBigMouse.
Vcp.Samsung.Status.AllowPrompt: Allow LittleBigMouse on the Samsung display…
Vcp.Hisense.Subtitle: Local network remote
Vcp.Hisense.PinNote: Select Request PIN: the projector will display the VIDAA app pairing code. SupportView, HomeKit and ConnectLife PINs are not compatible.
Vcp.Hisense.KeyMacroNote1: Try raw KEY_* names. A number after a key sets its delay in milliseconds.
Vcp.Hisense.KeyMacroNote2: Brightness candidates: KEY_BRIGHTNESSUP, KEY_BRIGHTNESSDOWN, KEY_BRIGHTNESS_CYCLE, KEY_BRIGHTNESS.
Vcp.Hisense.LaserNote1: The slider sends its 0–10 value as a raw numeric payload to this platform_service action.
Vcp.Hisense.LaserNote2: Candidates: changelaserluminance, changelaserbrightness, changeluminance, changebacklight, setlaserlevel, setlaserbrightness.
Vcp.Hisense.PictureNote1: Ask the projector for its own menu catalogue before trying an ID. A named laser setting is selected automatically below.
Vcp.Hisense.PictureNote2: Known IDs: 4 picture mode, 6 contrast, 7 software brightness. Avoid 50: it resets picture settings on some models.
Vcp.Hisense.MqttNote1: Start the continuous listener, then send picture settings or use the physical remote. Newest messages appear immediately at the top.
Vcp.Hisense.MqttNote2: Look for platform_service/data/picturesetting and its menu_id. Retained snapshots, duplicates, pairing messages and tokens are filtered and never saved.
